title: Boundary Condition dependent Universality Classes on a Hyperbolic Lattice
authors: Pallabi Dey, Debasish Banerjee, Arnab Kundu, Ritam Sinha
abstract: We study the ferromagnetic Ising model on finite hyperbolic tessellations of Euclidean AdS$_2$ with open and wired boundary conditions. Because a finite fraction of spins remains at the boundary as the lattice grows, these conditions select distinct thermodynamic behaviours. In the $\{5,4\}$ tessellation, Monte-Carlo simulations using efficient worm algorithms on open boundaries (OBC) yield a transition near $β_c J=0.632(3)$, with susceptibility data collapsing under scaling by the total number of spins $N$. The fitted finite-size exponents, $1/\barν \simeq 0.162$ and $γ/\barν \simeq 0.743$, differ substantially from the mean-field volume scaling. Wired boundaries (WBC), which correlate boundary spins, instead show a transition around $β_c J=0.348(4)$ to an ordered phase consistent with the mean-field exponents. While the mean-field criticality with WBC is consistent with previous studies and with the suppression of independent boundary fluctuations, the OBC exponents hint at the presence of a new universality class. Results from other tessellations support the robustness of the observed scaling with OBC. We discuss a possible route to interpolate between the different boundary conditions. Our findings show that boundary dynamics must be specified when characterizing critical behaviour on hyperbolic lattices.
summary: This work analyzes the critical behavior of the Ising model on hyperbolic lattices, finding that the choice of boundary condition (Open vs. Wired) dictates the resulting universality class. Using Monte-Carlo simulations and Finite-Size Scaling, the authors demonstrate that OBC leads to exponents deviating from mean-field theory, while WBC aligns with it, highlighting the critical role of boundary dynamics in curved geometries.
main_problem: The study investigates how different boundary conditions (Open vs. Wired) fundamentally alter the critical behavior and universality classes of the Ising model when placed on negatively curved hyperbolic lattices.
main_result: Open boundary conditions yield critical exponents distinct from mean-field predictions, suggesting a new universality class, while wired boundary conditions recover mean-field behavior, emphasizing that boundary dynamics must be specified for accurate characterization.
method: The research employs Monte-Carlo simulations combined with rigorous Finite-Size Scaling (FSS) analysis to extract critical coupling constants and scaling exponents.
model_or_system: The system is the ferromagnetic Ising model ($s_i = \pm 1$) simulated on finite hyperbolic tessellations of Euclidean AdS$_2$, specifically using the $\{5, 4\}$ geometry. The Hamiltonian is analyzed under both Open Boundary Conditions (OBC) and Wired Boundary Conditions (WBC).
important_parameters: The geometry is defined by the tessellation $\{p, q\}$ (e.g., $\{5, 4\}$), and the comparison is drawn between OBC and WBC regimes.
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that the critical behavior is sensitive to the boundary conditions, and the analysis relies on the validity of the FSS hypothesis for different boundary types.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the hyperbolic tessellation, spin configurations in different phases, and the collapse of susceptibility and Binder cumulant data under FSS for both OBC and WBC.
paper_structure: The paper systematically compares the critical behavior derived from OBC versus WBC on the hyperbolic lattice, using FSS to extract exponents, and concludes by arguing for the necessity of specifying boundary dynamics.
why_interesting: The explicit study of boundary effects on critical phenomena in curved spaces provides a model for understanding how boundary constraints can fundamentally alter bulk critical theories, which has parallels in open quantum systems.
